claims.text: DFT-based molecular dynamics using the Z-method can yield the melting temperature of high-melting refractory materials.
The Z-method can yield latent heat and the entropy and enthalpy of fusion.
The Z-method can yield the volume change at melting.
The Z-method has accuracy similar to full free-energy thermodynamic integration.
The Z-method has substantially lower computational cost than full free-energy thermodynamic integration.
In constant-energy NVE ab initio molecular dynamics, a crystal can be driven into a superheated state until spontaneous melting occurs.
Using a sufficiently large simulation cell minimizes finite-size effects.
The emergence and evolution of a solid-liquid interface mediate conversion of the superheated solid to a mixed-phase state.
At the crystalline lattice's metastability limit, the system abruptly transitions into a mixed solid-liquid state.
Melting in the Z-method produces a sudden temperature drop.
Concurrent energy and volume discontinuities quantify latent heat and other melting properties.
The simulation should exhibit a characteristic Z-curve consisting of superheating followed by a rapid temperature drop at melting.
Entropy of fusion can be derived from the latent heat and melting temperature.
Full ab initio free-energy calculations using thermodynamic integration provide a benchmark for validated melting properties.
The method is sensitive to finite-size effects and the choice of DFT exchange-correlation functional.
The method may fail to capture subtle kinetic barriers in materials with anomalously slow melting dynamics or strong anisotropy.
The Z-method is promising for high-throughput screening.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies an NVE simulation, in which volume is fixed, while the mechanism and outcome invoke a concurrent volume discontinuity and measurement of volume change across the transition. A volume change cannot be obtained directly within one fixed-volume NVE trajectory without additional simulations at different volumes or a separate equation-of-state procedure.
